findings.title: Missing Input Length Limits on Cover Letter jobDescription
findings.description: The jobDescription field in generateSchema is defined as z.string() without any max length validation. This allows clients to send arbitrarily large strings that could cause memory exhaustion or DoS.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a cover letter generation request with a multi-MB jobDescription field, causing the server to allocate excessive memory or timeout while processing.
findings.recommendation: Add max length validation: jobDescription: z.string().max(50000)

findings.title: PDF Content Validation Missing Magic Bytes Check
findings.description: validatePDF() only checks the mimetype from multer, which can be easily spoofed. The actual file content is not validated for PDF magic bytes (%PDF).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker uploads a malicious file with PDF extension and manipulated Content-Type header. The file is accepted even if not a valid PDF, potentially causing issues when pdf-parse processes it.
findings.recommendation: Add magic bytes validation: const buffer = Buffer.allocfers(5); fs.readSync(fd, buffer, 0, 5, 0); if (buffer.toString() !== '%PDF') return { valid: false }

findings.title: Prompt Injection Risk in Resume Parsing
findings.description: User-provided extractedText from resumes is directly interpolated into the AI prompt without sanitization. Malicious resume content could manipulate the AI response.
findings.attack_scenario: A user creates a resume with specially crafted content designed to make the AI ignore its instructions or output attacker-controlled data. The prompt includes: 'IMPORTANT: Only extract information that is clearly present in the resume. Do not guess or invent details. RESUME TEXT: {user-controlled}'
findings.recommendation: Implement prompt injection defenses: (1) Use system message framing, (2) Add content boundaries markers, (3) Sanitize/rescape control characters from extractedText before embedding in prompt

findings.title: Unvalidated Input Passed to Queue Jobs
findings.description: The jobDescription parameter in /:id/analyze is passed directly to the queue without validation. While it is optional (z.string().optional()), no length limit is enforced.
findings.attack_scenario: Large jobDescription values could be stored in the database or passed to background workers, causing resource exhaustion.

findings.title: Missing JSON Payload Size Limit on Generic Endpoints
findings.description: Express.json() middleware is used without an explicit 'limit' option, defaulting to 100KB. Large JSON payloads could bypass this on unguarded endpoints.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a massive JSON body to overwhelm the server parsing resources.

findings.title: API Key Storage Uses ECB Mode Encryption
findings.description: API keys are encrypted before storage. Need to verify encryption implementation does not use weak modes like ECB.
findings.attack_scenario: Weak encryption could be broken, exposing user API keys stored in the database.
findings.recommendation: Use AES-GCM or AES-CTR with random IVs. Avoid ECB mode entirely.

residual_risks.description: Several endpoints accept user input without strict allowlisting. The application relies on Zod for validation but some fields lack max length enforcement.
Resume parsing and job matching use external AI services. Prompt injection and response manipulation risks exist but are partially mitigated by default fallbacks.
PDF validation checks mimetype but not content. Magic bytes validation would strengthen security.
Rate limiters are configured but could be bypassed with distributed requests. Consider IP-based fail2ban for production.

testing_gaps.gap: Fuzz testing with malformed PDF files
testing_gaps.description: Test pdf-parse library behavior with malicious PDF payloads, password-protected PDFs, and corrupt files
Test resume parsing with various prompt injection patterns in resume text
Send max-size payloads to all endpoints to verify timeout and memory behavior
Test SSRF guard with new URL patterns, DNS rebinding attempts, and IPv6 variants
